body:
`wait_for_stable_file` (root/etc/s6-overlay/s6-rc.d/cwa-ingest-service/run:99)
decides a file has finished being written when two size samples
STABLE_INTERVAL apart are equal. Production defaults are STABLE_INTERVAL=0.5,
STABLE_CHECKS=6, STABLE_CONSEC_MATCH=2.

Two equal samples 0.5s apart do not prove the writer finished — only that it
wrote nothing in that window. A copy that stalls longer than 0.5s (slow or
contended network share, a paused download client, an NFS hiccup) is therefore
reported as settled, and the startup sweep hands a partially-written file to
handle_event. That is the exact symptom
test_startup_sweep_leaves_a_still_growing_file_to_the_watcher exists to
prevent, at production timings rather than test ones.

The inotify event path is partly protected — a bare CREATE on an nlink==1 file
is refused anyway — but the startup sweep calls handle_event directly.

Found while de-flaking that test in #1579 (its harness collides the probe
interval with its writer period, which is a separate, test-only defect and is
fixed there). Not fixed in that PR: changing ingest timing needs its own
evidence and a blast-radius trace across both callers, and no user has
reported a partial import from this path.

Possible directions, none verified: require more than two consecutive matching
samples at production defaults; gate on mtime age as well as size; or require a
close_write for sweep candidates the way the event path effectively does.

resolution.note: Production stability requires six 0.5-second size samples, exactly 2.5 seconds of unchanged size; live events retain CLOSE_WRITE protection, and the startup regression runs at production timings with a 1.1-second stalled writer.

title: wait_for_stable_file can declare a stalled copy settled
